title: What does an AI engineer do? A week inside Belvo's Intelligence team
summary: What does an AI engineer do? Spend a week with Belvo's Intelligence team and see how they build AI tools that help every team work smarter.
body_markdown:
Every morning, Belvo's Intelligence team gets together for its daily call across two time zones: three engineers in Brazil and one in Barcelona, who keep Brazil hours so the team can build in sync. What they build reaches far beyond their own code.


This is the team behind Belvo's AI workflows. Renan Cunha (Staff Software Engineer and team lead), Guilherme Marques, Pedro Camargo, and Arthur Moreno (Senior Software Engineers) build AI products for Belvo's customers. Just as important, they build the platform that lets every other team at Belvo, from Sales and Customer Success to People, put AI to work on its own.


Few companies have a team dedicated to making everyone else better at AI. At Belvo, that's a deliberate bet: AI should run through how every team works, decides, and serves customers, instead of living in one corner of the company. The Intelligence team turns that bet into everyday reality with shared tools, safe ways to run agents, and room to experiment. A salesperson, an analyst, or a recruiter can build with AI as naturally as an engineer, and the whole company moves faster for it.


We asked them to walk us through a regular week. Here's what Monday to Friday looks like.


## **Monday: how does an AI engineering team set its priorities?**


"We always have our team daily early in the morning," says Renan. From there, the work follows a prioritized list. "We use AI a lot," he adds, and that starts with the team's own routine: automated jobs, agents that open pull requests, and recurring checks that used to take up someone's morning.


That frees the team for the work that matters most. Operational emergencies are rare, and most of what they build has no playbook yet. Guilherme puts it this way:


"I think the challenge for our team in planning is navigating uncertainty, more than priorities." **Guilherme Marques, Senior Software Engineer**


So every week begins with choosing where to explore and what to test first. In his words, "it's very much a work of experimentation."


## **Tuesday: which AI tools do engineers use day to day?**


Tuesday is a building day, and engineers pick the tool that fits the job. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, are all on the table. Belvo doesn't lock the team into a single vendor, and nobody has to ask permission to keep going. When someone hits their token limit, their account is upgraded automatically, with no questions asked.


For Guilherme, building with AI has also changed what a "product" looks like:


"A product, a lot of the time, can be a skill and an MCP." **Guilherme Marques, Senior Software Engineer**


An MCP ([Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) ) is a standard way to connect AI assistants like Claude to tools and data. In plain words: instead of building a whole new interface, the team often gives people's existing AI assistants the right context and access, and lets them do the rest. Belvo has also launched MCPs of its own for customers, including an[official Claude connector](https://belvo.com/resources/mcps/) .


Speed comes easily with AI. What the team cares about is making sure every engineer understands and owns the code they ship, so quality keeps pace with velocity. As Guilherme says, "you have to have taste and judgment."


*Intelligence team at their first offsite in Barcelona.*


## **Wednesday: how does an AI platform team work with the rest of the company?**


"I think our team is a platform team," says Guilherme. Midweek is when that part of the job shows up most: the Intelligence team builds tools that other teams use on their own, and sometimes the fastest win doesn't involve a complex agent at all.


Pedro remembers a tool he put together for the Sales team. In two weeks, it sent more than 250 emails and was already booking meetings.


For Pedro, quick wins like this point to something bigger:


"We're heading toward a scenario where teams will have more autonomy." **Pedro Camargo, Senior Software Engineer**


Other examples are spread across the company. Anyone at Belvo can now query the company's data lake straight from Claude, Cursor, or Codex. Other examples are spread across the company. Anyone at Belvo can now query the company's data lake straight from Claude, Cursor, or Codex. And in a dedicated Slack channel, people chat with Data Mate, an agent that turns plain-language questions into answers from Belvo's data. Customer Success checks how an account is ramping up, Sales looks at usage trends before a call, and Solutions Engineers review the status of a payment in seconds. Before, the same question meant digging through a dashboard someone else built or opening a request with the data team and waiting in line.


Another Slack agent answers questions about[direct debit in Mexico](https://belvo.com/blog/direct-debit-digital-authorization/) and hands the conversation to a person whenever it isn't sure. And adoption isn't limited to engineers: Belvo's[non-technical teams](https://belvo.com/blog/from-hackathon-real-life-what-belvo-people-team-building-with-ai/) use AI at a level that's still rare in the market.


Wednesday is also a good day to talk about security. "We're with the security team all the time," says Renan. Because everything in this space is so new, the two teams build together. Intelligence designs the golden paths (the recommended, documented way to do something) and writes the documentation. Security adds the guardrails. Their current project together is a platform to run AI agents safely across the company.


## **Thursday: what's the hardest part of building AI for financial services?**


The team's answer is surprisingly human: helping people see what AI can do in their own reality.


"We started working with the day-zero customer," Renan explains. The idea is to solve one small, concrete pain and discover bigger problems from there. Credit Desk is the clearest example. It started with one lender's day-to-day analysis work and has been live in production since October, with a team of credit analysts reviewing thousands of loan proposals a week in Credit Desk instead of spreadsheets. Next up: more customers and more features.


Along the way, the team learned that many customers don't yet picture what AI could change in their own operations, so part of the job is showing them. For Renan, that has been one of the biggest lessons: knowing how to sell AI to customers matters as much as mastering the algorithms.


## **Friday: what's next for AI at Belvo?**


Fridays are for looking ahead. "We're investing in a few fronts," says Renan, and for him the opportunity lies in the data Belvo already has:


"In the coming year, there's a lot of value we can create on top of the data we already have." **Renan Cunha, Staff Software Engineer and Intelligence lead**


Pedro pictures where the platform is heading:


"I'm excited about the future of our platform with many, many agents. Autonomous and collaborative, and seeing a big fleet of agents running here on our platform. That's what I'm most excited about." **Pedro Camargo, Senior Software Engineer**


Guilherme is looking forward to what nobody has found yet:


"What excites me most are the discoveries we're still going to make. Which products are we still going to discover?" **Guilherme Marques, Senior Software Engineer**


He also expects that fleet of agents to reshape how everyone at Belvo works. "It's already changed, and now it's going to change even more," he says.


Pedro adds a lesson that shapes how the team builds for everyone else: "People use AI tools in different, individual ways." That's why the team builds platforms and golden paths instead of one rigid way of working.


"We're a relatively new team," Pedro says, and this week marks a milestone: the team just met in person for its[first offsite](https://belvo.com/blog/belvo-teams-offsite-world-is-our-office/) . For Pedro, it was the first time meeting his teammates face to face.


## **What is it like to work in AI at Belvo?**


Spend a week with the Intelligence team and Belvo's values stop being words on a careers page:


- **We get things done.** Start with one real problem, ship something useful, and grow from there.
- **Relentless curiosity.** No rigid gates or budgets for experimenting. Exploration is part of the daily routine.
- **Constant growth.** Engineers who joined to build AI are now also learning to explain it, sell it, and teach it.
- **Resilience.** Building where there are no ready-made answers means learning fast and adapting when plans change.
- **Fun-loving.** Taking on challenges bigger than ourselves, and enjoying the ride across Brazil, Mexico, and Spain.


All of this runs on trust. Engineers get access to the best tools, automatic upgrades when they need more capacity, and real investment in the infrastructure they rely on.


## **Who would thrive on Belvo's Intelligence team?**


Pedro sums it up: "Curiosity is fundamental to working on this team." Add to that someone who feels at home without a playbook, cares about quality as much as speed, enjoys explaining technology to people who don't write code, and gets excited when a tool they built becomes part of another team's routine.
